title: NBA Logo Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The NBA Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo?
description: A hard NBA logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of NBA team logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the team, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from an NBA team logo, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No basketball-shaped freebies, no team names. Each piece still holds one real detail, a color pair, a seam or an edge that only one team owns.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.piece: The orange and blue streaks under the shield.
items.fact: The Thunder logo debuted in 2008, the franchise's first season in Oklahoma City after leaving Seattle.

items.piece: The snowcapped mountain peak at the top of the circle.
items.fact: Denver's 2018 rebrand crossed two pickaxes over the mountain, a nod to the Colorado mining history behind the Nuggets name.

items.piece: The cables of the Bay Bridge.
items.fact: The bridge logo arrived in 2010 and was updated in 2019, the year the Warriors moved from Oakland to San Francisco.

items.piece: The black seams on the flaming basketball.
items.fact: The flaming ball dropping through a hoop has been the Heat's logo since their first season in 1988.

items.piece: Part of the CELTICS lettering that arches over the shamrock.
items.fact: The shamrock and the Celtics name both point to Boston's Irish roots; founder Walter Brown picked the name in 1946.

items.piece: The sun's rays meeting the bottom of the basketball.
items.fact: Phoenix's current sunburst-and-ball logo dates to a 2013 refresh of the mark the team has used in some form since 1968.

items.piece: The seams at the top of the gold basketball, just above LOS ANGELES.
items.fact: The name came from Minnesota, the Land of 10,000 Lakes. The Lakers kept it when they moved to Los Angeles in 1960.

items.piece: The black edge of the bull's red face, near the snout.
items.fact: The Bulls' logo has barely changed since the team's first season in 1966, one of the steadiest marks in sports.
